bottleneck: Not throughput. Canonical F1 NGRAM self-speculation is BUG_CONFIRMED at greedy t=0; the fault line between wrong verify-row context (A) and post-verify KV/state corruption (B) was unresolved, and the only real ON/OFF packet with complete top-8 (C21/C22) had not been used for a row-level commit-consistency audit. Without that audit, the next fix would be chosen from an unvalidated mechanism.
hypothesis: H-D: at every reported output position the committed token equals the argmax of the top-8 row reported for the same position (greedy t=0 contract). If ON violates this while OFF does not, a commit/slot-read fault (B-like) is indicated; if ON is universally self-consistent, the wrong token is already the argmax of a mis-contextualized verify row (A-like). Secondary H-E: reported rows are a deterministic function of the committed token prefix, so ON-vs-OFF logprob gaps can localize the fault. EXECUTED RESULT: H-D holds in 959/960 positions; the single exception is an exact tie (ids 48977 and 1271 both at logprob -1.556087613105774, A/repeat-512/c4same instance 3 position 6), so there is no token/row mismatch beyond a tie. H-E is FALSIFIED: same-prompt ON requests with identical committed-token prefixes report rows differing by up to 3.39 nats over a 4-6 token shared prefix, and the pair with a fully identical 48-token output (B/c4same 1 vs 3) differs by up to 5.157 nats (median 1.750), while row 0 is bit-identical in all 12 pairs. The reported verify row is therefore not determined by the committed prefix; it depends on non-committed (draft-tree / KV / position) state, with a sharp onset after position 4 for the full-identical pair.
patch: No engine change (analysis-only iteration). Added g3-t12/analyze_ngram_pairs.py and preserved raw derived output g3-t12/raw/self_consistency.json, g3-t12/raw/same_prefix_control.json, g3-t12/raw/run_stdout.txt. The script reads the Controller-supplied ngram-full-observations.json read-only (sha256 pinned in output), asserts length/shape invariants, computes per-position commit-vs-row-argmax, the exact-tie case, ON/OFF first-divergence structure, and the same-prefix ON-vs-ON row-delta control. Originals untouched; no fabricated measurements.
tests: EXECUTED (CPU, stdlib only, python3 -I): g3-t12/analyze_ngram_pairs.py exit 0 on the real 20-response packet (10 ON/OFF pairs, 960 positions, complete chosen + top-8). Primary results: (1) 960/960 positions self-consistent up to one exact logprob tie; (2) 12 same-prompt ON-vs-ON pairs: row 0 delta = 0.0 everywhere; six pairs reach 2.88-3.39 nats over 4-6 shared-prefix positions; four pairs stay <=0.16 nats; the full 48-token identical-output pair reaches 5.157 nats with small deltas only at positions 0-4 and 13. Limits: single packet, two prompts (A/B repeat-512), 48 output tokens, no GPU, no per-step draft ids, no accepted-node indices, no KV/position dumps, no accept_len==1 intervention. REQUESTED (custom diagnostic, NOT a fast gate, request_fast_gate=false): two identical single-request NGRAM-ON runs at the same commit/prompt/seed with per-verify-step logging of positions, tree-mask rows, accept_lens, accept_index/retrieve_index and reported top-8 rows. Discrimination: identical single requests differ -> request-level nondeterminism independent of concurrency; they agree but C4-same requests differ -> batch-slot/state coupling; instrument host-vs-device seq_lens/positions and compare the first divergent row against the row implied by the committed prefix. Bounds: one prompt, 48 output tokens, 2 runs, logs only, no scoring or timing comparison.
learning: The complete real packet corrects two prior readings. First, the commit is self-consistent with its own reported row in 959/960 positions, and the only exception is an exact logprob tie, so trial-3's partial-sample suggestion that ON sometimes commits a token different from its own top-1 is not reproduced; the fault is upstream of the commit, in how the verify row is computed or which hidden state it reads. Second, the magnitude of ON-vs-OFF logprob gaps cannot localize that upstream fault: same-prefix ON-vs-ON requests show equal or larger gaps (up to 5.16 nats over 48 identical committed tokens), with prefill row 0 bit-identical. This is a bounded negative methodological finding: reported top-k gaps are confounded by hidden-state dependence on non-committed draft/KV state. The packet cannot distinguish tree-mask/position leakage from KV-move corruption, and no root cause, fix, numeric equivalence, speedup or promotion is claimed.
next_proposal: Run the bounded custom NGRAM-ON repeatability diagnostic described in tests (same single request twice, per-step positions/mask/accept-index/top-8 logging; no scoring, no speed claim). Decision tree: (a) identical requests differ at the same prefix position -> request-level nondeterminism in verify state; then instrument host-vs-device seq_lens/positions and the KV-move slot mapping at the boundary, since the full-identical pair's row jump starts at position 5 after a near-identical position-4 row. (b) identical requests agree but concurrent C4-same requests differ -> batch-slot/state coupling; compare positions and tree-mask rows per slot and check whether the row for an accepted node depends on non-ancestor draft nodes. (c) if the first divergent row cannot be reproduced from the committed prefix under any mask/position hypothesis, dump the moved KV for accepted positions and compare it against the verify-forward KV before any fix is proposed. Do not promote NGRAM; quality budget stays open; do not re-run the missing-top-k field probe (C5/C7 closed).
uncertainty: UNRESOLVED_FAULT_LINE: not established whether the non-committed state dependence is in the tree mask/positions, the KV move, or batching. The analysis is finite (2 prompts, repeat-512, 48 output tokens, 10 pairs), CPU-only, and derives from the Controller packet rather than a fresh engine run. No accept_len==1 control exists. Self-consistency up to one exact tie does not prove the row is correct; it only shows the commit matches the row the engine reports. No promotion, EXACT, performance or quality claim is made.
